title: Dimension of the affine Kummer image
as_he_states: The diagram asks whether the image has dimension n+1, with the n-reading itself doubtful.
plausible_today: For r independent nonzero algebraic generators over a number field, the scalar affine image after a finite splitting-field extension is open, so each ℓ-adic component has Lie dimension r+1. The phrase dimension needs this explicit interpretation; the adelic image is not a finite-dimensional algebraic variety.
state_of_art: PeruccaSgobba2019 Theorem 1.1, p.1617, gives the uniform number-field Kummer degree bound. The bounded finite-level affine indices prove openness; its ℓ-adic projection has dimension r+1. MoreeStevenhagen2014 Theorem 2.5 gives the stronger exact intrinsic index 2^r over Q.
why_open: The page records a question, with no reason for leaving it open; later exact radical descriptions settle the rational split formulation. No claim that the present theorem first arose in2014 is made.
worth: Worth a short explanatory companion calculation; it is a settled normalization issue, not a new open theorem.

title: Finite index for independent algebraic Kummer generators
as_he_states: For quantities independent overZ modulo roots of unity, is the affine arithmetic image of finite index?
plausible_today: For a number field K and r independent nonzero algebraic generators in K*, the compatible radical image is open in the scalar affine group; for a torus pass first to a finite splitting field and retain its character-module action on descent. For Γ⊂Q* of rank r, the intrinsic saturated radical automorphism group has exact index 2^r. The same exact value is not asserted over arbitrary K.
state_of_art: Perucca–Sgobba2019 Theorem 1.1, published p.1617, proves a uniform bound for the failure of maximal Kummer degree over K(ζ_n). Its statement was opened in the World Scientific publisher preview; bounded finite-level affine indices give the desired openness. Moree–Stevenhagen2014 Theorem 2.5 gives the stronger exact rational saturated index 2^r and quadratic pairing. Perissinotto–Perucca2023 Theorems 1.1–1.2 give explicit degree procedures for products of one-dimensional tori.
why_open: The manuscript does not explain why the calculation stops. Backward search reached Schinzel1977 Theorem 2, whose statement at pp.245–246 was opened, and a Ribet1979 reference whose complete original was not read. The documentary date of this packet remains insecure, so no priority or first-settlement claim is made.
worth: Worth a bounded synthesis comparing the manuscript’s coordinate choice with the saturated radical lattice; the theorem itself is established.
